CORE WEB VITALS

Core Web Vitals: Google's Technical Standard Every Website Must Meet

Core Web Vitals are Google’s official performance benchmarks, and any serious web design services team builds to hit them from day one. Miss these targets and your rankings suffer, your bounce rate climbs, and your visitors leave before they ever see your offer.

Digital Marketing — The Full Ecosystem

  • LCP (Largest Contentful Paint): measures loading performance. Target under 2.5 seconds for a Good score
  • INP (Interaction to Next Paint): measures page responsiveness. Target under 200 milliseconds for a Good score
  • CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift): measures visual stability. Target under 0.1 for a Good score
  • FCP (First Contentful Paint): time until first content appears. Target under 1.8 seconds
  • TTFB (Time to First Byte): server response time. Target under 800 milliseconds
  • Page Speed Score: Google PageSpeed Insights score. Target 90+ on mobile and desktop
  • Mobile Usability: no mobile usability errors flagged in Google Search Console
  • Cumulative Layout Stability: zero layout shifts from ads, images, or late-loading elements
  • Efficient Image Loading: images in next-gen formats like WebP or AVIF with proper lazy loading
  • Minimal Render-Blocking Resources: critical CSS inlined, JavaScript deferred or async

Social Media Marketing — Platform-Focused

  • Ignoring Core Web Vitals, since Google uses them as active ranking factors in search results
  • Using unoptimized images, the number-one cause of slow loading websites everywhere
  • Loading excessive third-party scripts like tracking pixels, chat widgets, and plugins that pile on load time
  • Running large JavaScript bundles that block the main thread and delay page interactivity
  • Neglecting server response time, since slow hosting directly impacts TTFB and overall performance
  • Allowing layout shifts from fonts, images, and ads that load late and cause disruptive jumps
  • Skip mobile performance testing — desktop speed scores do not reflect mobile performance
  • Ignore Google Search Console warnings — Core Web Vitals issues are reported in real-time
  • Assume a fast desktop experience means a fast mobile experience — they are very different
  • Use page builders without performance optimization — unconfigured builders add bloat

Frequently Asked Questions

Common Questions About Web Design Services and What to Expect When Working with Zoot

1. How long does it take to design and build a website?

A standard business website typically takes 4-8 weeks from kickoff to launch, depending on complexity and how quickly you provide feedback and approvals. eCommerce websites and complex sites with custom functionality can take 8-16 weeks. We provide a detailed project timeline during the proposal stage so you know exactly what to expect.

2. What platform do you build websites on?

We primarily build on WordPress — the world's most popular CMS, powering over 40% of all websites. WordPress gives you full control over your content, is highly scalable, and has the best SEO capabilities of any platform. For eCommerce, we use WooCommerce on WordPress or Shopify depending on your requirements.

3. Will I be able to update my website myself?

Yes. We build all websites with easy-to-use page builders (Elementor) and provide training so you can make content updates, add blog posts, and make basic changes yourself without needing to know code. For more complex updates, our support team is always available to help.

4. Do you design custom websites or use templates?

We design fully custom websites — not templates or pre-built themes. Every design is created from scratch based on your brand identity, business goals, and target audience. This ensures your website is unique, on-brand, and optimized specifically for your conversion goals.

5. Will my website be mobile-friendly?

Absolutely. All our websites are designed mobile-first and tested across all screen sizes and devices before launch. We ensure your website looks and performs flawlessly on smartphones, tablets, and desktops — critical since the majority of web traffic now comes from mobile devices.

6. Do you handle website hosting?

Yes. We can manage hosting setup and configuration on your preferred hosting provider, or recommend a fast, reliable hosting solution for your website. We work with quality hosting providers and can manage the technical setup so you don't have to worry about server configuration.

7. What information do I need to provide for my website?

We guide you through the entire content collection process with a structured questionnaire covering your business, services, target audience, and design preferences. You'll need to provide your logo, brand guidelines (if existing), and any specific images or content you want to include. We handle all design and copywriting from there.

9. What happens after my website launches?

We provide a 30-day post-launch support period to fix any issues that arise. We also offer ongoing website maintenance packages that include regular updates, security monitoring, backups, and technical support. For continued growth, we recommend pairing your new website with our SEO and digital marketing services.

10. How much does a website design cost?

Website design pricing depends on the number of pages, complexity, functionality, and platform. A standard business website typically starts from ₹50,000, while complex eCommerce sites and custom builds are priced higher. Contact us for a detailed quote based on your specific requirements and business goals.

11. What are Core Web Vitals and why do they matter for my website?

Core Web Vitals are Google's set of specific metrics that measure real-world user experience on your website: Largest Contentful Paint (LCP) measures loading performance, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) measures responsiveness to user interactions, and Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) measures visual stability. Google uses these metrics as ranking factors — a website with poor Core Web Vitals scores will rank lower in search results compared to a faster, more stable competitor site. At Zoot, we build every website to meet or exceed Google's "Good" thresholds for all three Core Web Vitals.

12. Can you redesign my website without losing my current SEO rankings?

Yes. SEO-safe website redesigns require careful planning — mapping all existing URLs and implementing 301 redirects for any that change, preserving on-page SEO elements (title tags, meta descriptions, heading structure), maintaining existing internal linking architecture, and monitoring rankings closely post-launch. We conduct a pre-redesign SEO audit and implement a full redirect plan to protect your organic rankings. In most cases, our redesigns actually improve SEO performance by improving site speed, mobile experience, and technical SEO foundations.

13. Can I see examples of websites you have designed?

Yes. We have an extensive portfolio of website design projects across healthcare, legal, eCommerce, SaaS, hospitality, professional services, and more. Please visit our portfolio page or contact us and we'll share case studies and live examples most relevant to your industry. We're happy to walk you through specific projects, explain the design decisions made, and share the conversion and traffic results achieved after launch.

14. What is the difference between a website template and a custom design?

A template is a pre-built design that many businesses purchase and customize with their own content and branding. Templates are cheaper and faster but come with significant limitations: you cannot change the fundamental layout, your site looks similar to thousands of other businesses, and template code is often bloated and slow. A custom design is built from scratch specifically for your business — unique layout, optimized code, no design constraints, and a site that is purpose-built to convert your specific audience. We exclusively design custom websites because templates undermine the credibility, performance, and conversion rates your business deserves.
